selections.name: Octavius
selections.rationale: Octavius, who arrives ten days later and camps opposite Brutus at Philippi, is Octavian, the future Augustus, Antony's triumviral colleague. The graph entity Augustus lists 'Caesar Octavianus' as an alias, and the passage context (Antony facing Cassius) fits the Philippi campaign.

detail: Caesar's commemoration of the victory at Actium: dedications to Apollo of Actium from the captured ships, a larger temple, and the Actia games. (Cassius Dio 51.1.2, flagged)
interpretation: Dio explains why he gives the date of the battle: he reckons Caesar's sole rule, and so the years of his reign, from that day. (Cassius Dio 51.1.2, flagged)
